docs.dice.component: d4, d6 and d20 — documented in the kit's catalog, built by a SEPARATE package, `@game-presets/dice`. The add-on ships the kinds (sides, silhouettes seen from above), the face textures (SVG data URIs, as the cards add-on does), the classic skin and the throws. The engine carries the atom (`Rollable`), the verb (`roll`), the tumble and the ballistics — and nothing of what a die looks like.

A throw is TWO things kept apart on purpose. The RESULT is `Outcome`, one door with three sides: a **number** (the server said, the test pins, the cheat wants), **`{ seed }`** (every client draws the same face from the same seed), **`{ rng }`** (the game's own chance). The LOOK is the clock's: `rollDie` tumbles in place, `throwDie` slides across the desk on the ballistics (spin, friction, the walls of a tray) and writes where it stopped into the tree, `throwFromCarry` is the same throw with the finger's own speed — a drag let go with momentum. Every one commits the face through `showFace`, truth and picture together — and every one FLICKERS on the way (`flashFace`, the picture without the truth): the runtime cues a new face each time the die has turned or slid far enough to have gone over, so the cadence is the die's own motion and dies out with it, and the result is simply the last face the flicker shows.
const d = die("d20", { kind: "d20", at: { x: 0, y: 0 } })
throwDie(motions, desk, d, { speed: 9, angle: 15, spin: 900, walls: wallsOf(desk, tray), outcome: 17 })   // the server said 17
throwDie(motions, desk, d, { speed: 9, angle: 15, outcome: { seed: 42 } })                                  // every client lands the same
The dice are imported by package name, like any consumer — never a path into the add-on's src.
docs.dice.faces: Every face of every kind, as the classic skin draws them: the tetrahedron from above (a triangle, its numeral), the cube (a soft square, pips — the one and the centre of odd faces red, the printed convention), the icosahedron (a hexagon, the top face a triangle, its numeral; 6 and 9 underlined). Thirty surfaces, registered under speaking names (`dice/d6/classic/4`); swap the record behind one and every die showing that face changes at once.
docs.dice.roll: A tumble in place, with the result from any door. `outcome` picks where the face comes from — `seed`, `given`, `rng`. TAP THE DIE to roll it (on the panel, `rolled` does the same). The face is decided the moment the roll is asked, and on the way there the die shows face after face: a cue every 60° of turning, so the flicker thins out with the tumble and the result is the LAST face, landed while it is still turning. The truth changes once — the flicker is a picture (`flashFace`), and a rule reading the die mid-throw is never told a number nobody rolled. A tap walks the seed on (`seed + taps`); `rolled` does not, and the same seed lands the same face, which is the point of it.
docs.dice.script: A throw BY SCRIPT — what a game does on "the server rolled 17": `throwDie` slides the die across the tray on the engine's ballistics, the walls being the tray's own footprint (`wallsOf`), spinning and slowing by the tuning's `friction`/`spinFriction`/`bounce`; when it stops the seat is WRITTEN into the tree in the tray's own units. The face goes over on the die's OWN travel the whole way — a new one every half unit slid and every 60° spun — so the flicker dies out with the slide and the result is on the glass BEFORE it stops, never swapped onto a die standing still. TAP THE DIE to throw it; on the panel, `thrown` does the same (a tap walks the seed on).
docs.dice.throw: A throw BY HAND — drag the die and LET GO WHILE MOVING: the carry spring's speed at release becomes the slide's (`throwFromCarry`), scaled by `gain`; a slow release is a drop and the die stays put. The wiring is the catalog's ordinary drag with one hook: `onRelease` reads the finger's speed and hands the die to the clock's `slide` instead of the ordinary drop.
